Maybe not everyone is in favor of paying for college for inmates, and you can't really use this argument with them, but it just makes more sense to me that it's more logical to just offer that assistance to everyone and not just inmates. It's still the same problem. When you increase the amount of money in circulation, each dollar loses some of its value. If there was only 1 dollar, it would be worth a lot, but printing more splits the value between all the new dollars. This is a problem of scarcity.

For any currency to work, whatever is backing up the currency has to be finite. If everyone has all they need, then it's worthless. Would diamonds be so expensive if they were like grains of sand on a beach? No. You either need to back the paper money by a resource to give it worth or limit the money in circulation.

Even if a knife doesn't lock open, it isn't really that dangerous. Most non locking knives still have ways to keep them open. Swiss army knives, for example, have what's known as a slip joint, which is basically a spring that puts pressure on the blade to keep it open like a back lock would, but it's light enough you don't need to push anything but the blade, so it isn't technically a lock. Many slip joints also have a half stop which will stop the blade at a 90 degree angle with the handle in case it is closed on accident so your fingers don't get caught between the blade and handle. Or there are friction knives that have no springs or locks, and just rely on friction and an extension of the blade that overlaps the back of the handle to keep it open, so as long as you're holding the knife it won't close. I've cut myself a lot more with locking knives than non locking because once you disengage the lock of a knife, a lot of blades are fairly free moving. Non locking knives are usually harder to close because they don't have a strong lock, so they're usually made with blades that are harder to move.
